species.name: Northern pike
why: Water 47°F on top, much colder than they like, so they move slowly and stay deep.
Best water today is 2–20 ft deep, mostly on flats.
The lake is layered: warm water down to about 55 ft, cold below.
West wind at 10 mph pushes bait onto the east shore: try the wind-blown banks.

species.name: Walleye
why: Water 47°F on top, much colder than they like, so they move slowly and stay deep.
Best water today is 8–32 ft deep, mostly on channel edges.

Clear water: they bite best at dawn, dusk and on cloudy days.
